title: 10. Exercises: Multiprocessing Communication
summary: Next: 07_multiprocessing_pools.md — Learn about Process Pools and parallel execution →
objectives: Solve the Multiprocessing Communication exercises without looking at the lesson
Test edge cases and explain your approach

sections.title: Exercises
sections.body:
### Exercise 1: Multi-Producer Multi-Consumer

Create a system with:

1. 3 producer processes generating random numbers
2. 2 consumer processes computing squares
3. 1 aggregator process computing the sum
4. Use queues for communication

### Exercise 2: Chat System with Pipes

Create a two-process chat:

1. Each process can send and receive
2. Use bidirectional pipe
3. Display messages with timestamps
4. Graceful shutdown with "quit" command

### Exercise 3: Distributed Word Count

Count words in parallel:

1. Split a large text file into chunks
2. Each process counts words in its chunk
3. Combine results using Manager dict
4. Display top 10 words

### Exercise 4: Shared Progress Tracker

Create a progress tracking system:

1. Multiple worker processes
2. Shared Value for total progress
3. Shared Array for per-worker progress
4. Main process displays progress bar

### Exercise 5: Request-Response Server

Create a calculator server:

1. Server process handles requests via Pipe
2. Client processes send (operation, args)
3. Server returns results
4. Handle multiple operations: add, sub, mul, div

### Exercise 6: Parallel Sum

Calculate sum of large array:

1. Create shared Array of 1 million integers
2. Split into chunks for N workers
3. Each worker sums its chunk
4. Combine partial sums

### Exercise 7: Shared Cache

Implement a shared cache:

1. Manager dict as cache storage
2. Multiple worker processes
3. Workers check cache before computing
4. Measure cache hit rate

### Exercise 8: Pipeline Pattern

Create a data pipeline:

1. Stage 1: Generate numbers (Queue)
2. Stage 2: Square them (Queue)
3. Stage 3: Sum results (Value)
4. Each stage is a process

### Exercise 9: Broadcast Communication

Implement broadcast:

1. One sender process
2. Multiple receiver processes
3. Sender broadcasts to all receivers
4. Use Pipes or shared memory

### Exercise 10: Lock-Free Progress

Create lock-free progress:

1. Use Array for per-process counters
2. No locks (each process has own index)
3. Main reads all counters for total
4. Compare performance with locked version
